title: DirectorPlan
description: The director's constrained staging decisions for one scene (docs/planning/DIRECTOR-ROLE-PLAN.md, 2026-08-10 decision): a genuinely separate artifact from SceneIntent, not a replacement shape. Per-section camera framing/subject and per-actor arrival/departure blocking inform SceneIntent's existing shot_intents[].framing/subject_actor_id and actors[].arrives/departs fields -- resolve_intent.py and SceneSpec do not change shape for this. motion_note captures free-text mid-scene movement the script describes (e.g. 'flies into asteroid field') for human review only; no resolver mechanism consumes it yet.

dramatic_intent.description: One short phrase: what this scene is dramatically about. Human-review context only, not consumed downstream.

order.description: Matches the script section index this shot covers.

framing.description: Same vocabulary as SceneIntent.shot_intents[].framing -- no new camera-intent vocabulary; reuses the existing rail.

subject_actor.description: Cast member (lowercase dialogue-cue name) this shot centers on. Only meaningful when framing is close_on/medium_on; must be a cast member actually present in this scene.

purpose.description: Human-readable reason for this shot choice, e.g. 'reveal', 'reaction', 'emphasize order'.

motion_note.description: Free-text mid-scene movement the script describes for this section, if any -- always captured for human review even when it doesn't resolve into a move (below).

move.description: A mid-scene relocation this section's action text describes (e.g. 'flies into the asteroid field') that resolves to one of the location's actual marks -- informs SceneIntent.beats[].moves (docs/planning/DIRECTOR-ROLE-PLAN.md's mid-scene move mechanism). Omit entirely when the text doesn't clearly describe movement to a specific place, or when no available mark plausibly matches -- do not invent one.

actor.description: Cast member (lowercase dialogue-cue name) doing the moving; must be present in this scene.

to_mark.description: Must be exactly one of the marks given for this scene's location -- never a name you make up.

evidence.description: A short exact quote copied from the scene's own action text supporting this move.

actor.description: Cast member (lowercase dialogue-cue name), must be present in this scene.

arrives.description: Actor enters on foot at scene start -- same meaning as SceneIntent.actors[].arrives.

departs.description: Actor exits on foot at scene end -- same meaning as SceneIntent.actors[].departs.

evidence.description: A short exact quote copied from the scene's own action text supporting arrives/departs; empty string if both are false. A claimed flag whose evidence isn't an actual substring of the scene text is discarded -- this is the grounding check that lets free-form phrasing (not just a fixed keyword list) count, without trusting an unverified assertion.
